svg.title: HSM Core Service Architecture
svg.desc: Centralized encryption service using Azure Key Vault HSM with DEK/KEK envelope encryption pattern, plus the Tier 3 Bulk PoC (POST /dek/issue and /dek/unwrap on CORE SERVICE itself, paired with the separate hsm-bulk-client), dek_name reuse, BULK File's ciphertext-format interoperability with CORE SERVICE's own /decrypt (guarded by CoreBulkFileInteropTest), admission control (classification governance + kek_registry dek_name reservation, both shadow-mode-then-enforce), and the Python reference clients (examples/python) with their 3 supported auth modes
svg.text: Bearer JWT + end_user_id · client calls after PBAC ALLOW
Service SPN: read · Rotation SPN: write
Separate K8S service · HSM Service SPN
Generate: DEK = random_bytes(32) (or reuse via dek_name)
EDEK = KEK.wrap(DEK) → stored in EDEK Store
Response: { ciphertext } ← only field client needs to store
grant check → Redis HIT (skip KV) / MISS → KV unwrap → AES-GCM
Response: { plaintext } ← only field client needs
Rotation SVC: gen bytes → write inactive slot → update current_key
Pods poll 30s: detect slot or kv_version change → rotate(cek, slot, ver)
Redis key: {slot}:{kv_ver}:{edek_id} · prev slot readable via fallback
Old {slot}:{old_ver}:* entries expire via 60s TTL — no flush needed
Same per-item crypto path, looped — no new EDEK-writing path
N items/call, keyed by caller's own id · cap = batch-max-items (100)
Always 200 · per-item status success/error (bad batch itself → 422)
Not part of the encryption solution
same edek_records table · same process as /decrypt
batch job on hsm-crypto-client — shared by hsm-spark-adapter
plaintext never leaves CLNT's host; real KEK never seen
dek-name on a column: ONE /dek/issue for
the whole job run, not once per row
TokenProvider: static, Azure AD, self-signed JWT, or mTLS
Workload Identity, or a local keypair — renewal never leaves CLNT
CORE SERVICE's real /decrypt reads it as-is
Bearer (3 modes) or mTLS client cert + X-App-ID
BULK File job: each chunk's plaintext base64-encoded before AES-256-GCM — survives CORE SERVICE's own /decrypt UTF-8 response encoding losslessly
FileBulkJob.reconstructCoreServiceToken(edek_id, iv, tag, ciphertext) — same token format CORE SERVICE itself produces, now true for files too
Optional compress-before-encrypt: gzip + 1-byte marker inside the AEAD payload, before base64 — decrypt always reads it, no config to coordinate
CoreBulkFileInteropTest (hsm-bulk-client) — real CORE SERVICE process, both endpoint shapes + compression, every build
Two independent, phased (shadow-mode → enforce) checks — both fresh-mint-only, both never run on reuse or /decrypt
Checked at first-mint (declaring app) AND cross-app reuse (grantee app) —
a dek_name grant answers WHICH key; this answers WHAT classification label
kek_registry · schema: hsm_crypto · same table as KEK selection (V11)
Only exact-dek_name rows (data_classification=UNSET) carry reservation intent
— classification-tier / per-app-default rows never do (no specific name)
DekNameReservationService · kek_registry was KEK-selection-only, V11-V14, before this round
New admin endpoints (this table/mechanism previously had NO admin API — direct DB/seed access only):
read-only ownership/metadata lookup — resolves cross-app decrypt denials [manage_apps]
kek_registry CRUD, incl. tier-1 dek_name reservations [manage_kek_registry]
Both checks always executed on a fresh mint regardless of enforce — the flag only gates throw-vs-log; audit event either way (status=denied or conflict_shadow_mode)
hsm_core_batch_file.py · hsm_bulk_file_reader.py — no JVM required, built for an Azure Function decrypt-validation path
decrypt_bulk_file: reads a REAL FileBulkJob file, decrypts via
e.g. a Function's own managed identity) — MTLS not supported (TLS-layer)
Same 3-of-4 AuthMode subset hsm-databricks-udf already supports (SELF_SIGNED_JWT verified there too, tests/test_live_interop.py) — AZURE_AD is new here,
ported from hsm-crypto-client's own SvcConfig.AuthMode (the Java reference for all 4 modes, used by the hsm-bulk-client (CLNT) box above)
Drives the same wire format as ENCRYPT/DECRYPT PAYLOAD FLOW (left) and hsm-bulk-client's own FileBulkJob output — zero adapter, zero re-encryption
No AUTHZ-specific test coverage yet (grants/classification/reservation denial paths) — only wire-format/interop verified live, see this directory's README
